segments.text: Welcome back to GitHub. Awesome. Two weeks off, now back at it. GitHub trending today, episode 34. 35 trending
open-source projects on GitHub right now. Let's get into it.
Using AI coding tools all day with no feedback on whether your prompting is actually improving is the norm for most
developers. AI Engineer Coach is a VS Code extension from Microsoft that reads your local AI session logs across
Claude, Codeex, and Xcode and turns them into actionable insights, tracks your practice scores over time, and flags prompts you repeat often enough to turn into reusable skills.
Google's Magic Pointer is Chromebook only. AI pointer brings it to every OS.
Wiggle your mouse or hit a hotkey and a glass morphism overlay appears right next to your cursor. It screenshots whatever you're pointing at and feeds it
to a vision model. Type or speak your question in any of seven languages. Get your answer without switching tabs or copying anything. Bring your own key.
Anthropic, OpenAI, or Gemini.
AI coding agents need to drive terminal apps, but most CLI tools were never designed to be controlled programmatically. Armox is a universal
Rust multiplexer with a typed SDK that lets you spawn, read, write, and control any CLI or TUI app from code. Native on
Linux, Mac OS, and Windows. No T-Mux or screen dependency. Your agent can drive HTTOP, Vim, PSQL, or any other terminal program as if it had hands.
Most computer use agents start from scratch every session. Photo agents is built to actually learn. It's an
autonomous self-evolving agent framework that uses vision grounded layered memory. So, it sees your screen the way
a human would. The really interesting part is that it writes its own skills.
Every time it successfully completes a task, it codifies that knowledge and reuses it next time. Gets better.
Most coding agents are bloated Python processes that eat RAM before they've written a single line of code. ZeroStack
is the opposite. A minimalistic coding agent written in Rust built around one obsession, memory footprint and
performance. No heavy runtime, no unnecessary dependencies, just a lean agent that reads your codebase, calls
your LLM, and gets out of the way. Your terminal app has a built-in AI that reads your code, writes diffs, runs
agents, and never phones home. That's Terra. It's 7 megabytes. Rust backend, React front end works with OpenAI,
Anthropic, Groak, or a fully local model through LM Studio. Multitab terminal, file explorer, code editor with Vim mode. All in one window. No account, no
telemetry. Your API keys go straight to the OS keychain.
Every AI coding agent today burns through tokens like there's no tomorrow.
And your API bill at the end of the month proves it. Open Skilla is an open-source AI agent designed for token
efficiency, getting more intelligence per dollar out of the same budget.
Smarter context management, leaner prompts, more useful output per call. If you're running agents at scale, and the cost is killing your runway, this one's
worth a look. You leave Claude Code running for 2 hours and have no idea if it's actually working or just frozen.
Open Pets is a desktop pet that lives on your screen and reflects what your AI coding agent is actually doing in real time. Connect Cloud Code through MCP.
Install whatever pet you want and watch it react as your agent codes, thinks, or sits idle. The '9s desktop buddy aesthetic meets modern AI workflows.
Most multimodal AI models either understand visuals or generate them.
Bite Dance open-sourced Lance, a single 3B parameter model that does both plus editing across images and video. It
scores highest on VBench among all unified models, beating Show O2 at 7B with less than half the parameters. A dual stream mixture of experts
architecture keeps understanding and generation pathways separate without splitting them into different models.
Your Android phone is running a powerful ARM chip that spends most of its time displaying notifications. Droid turns it into a real Linux desktop with two shell scripts, Termox, Termox X11 and Pr.
Direct kernel access, no emulation. Plug into a monitor and run VS Code, Libri Office, Blender, or a local AI model.
Unplug and your entire setup comes with you. A full Linux workstation that fits in your pocket.
Claude code and cursor assume you're running a frontier model with an infinite context budget. Small code assumes you're not. It's an AI coding
agent built specifically for small LLMs, hitting 87% on ESTAB bench with a 4B active parameter model designed to get
maximum coding performance out of the models that actually run locally on your hardware. If you're serious about local AI development, this one belongs on your radar.
Codeex prompts that work great suddenly break when you paste them into clawed code and vice versa.
Agents best practices is built to end that. It's a provider neutral agent skill covering harness design patterns that work across codecs, claude code,
and other coding agents. One set of practices, one shared way to think about prompts, tools, and context regardless of which model is on the other end.
AI agents write code now, but they are still using languages built for humans.
Versel dropped zero. It is a systems language explicitly designed for AI agents. Instead of printing normal console errors, the compiler spits out
structured JSON so the agent knows exactly how to fix its own bugs. I genuinely do not know if giving bots their own programming language is brilliant or terrifying.
Every time you switch from S3 to Cloudflare R2 or Versel blob, you rewrite your storage code from scratch.
Files SDK ends that one unified TypeScript SDK with a single honest API that works across S3, R2, Versa Blob,
Superbase, and more. Web standards.io, tree shakable, zero lockin. Write your upload and download logic once, swap the back end in config.
Discord eats 800 megabytes of RAM just to show you text messages. Concord runs the entire thing in your terminal using
20 to 40 megabytes built in Rust. It's a full Discord client with servers, channels, threads, DMs, polls,
reactions, and inline image previews using the Kitty or iTerm2 graphics protocols. Vim style navigation, fuzzy
channel search, file paste to upload, and desktop notifications.
Autopreso transcribes your speech in real time and generates slides or whiteboard sketches as you talk. Say the
thing. Watch the diagram appear. No fumbling through keynote. No stopping to draw. Technical interviews, brainstorming sessions, any meeting
where thinking out loud is faster than preparing slides. The whiteboard that whiteboards itself.
You finished your app, recorded a demo, and now it just looks like a raw iPhone screen capture. Maya makes it look like
a launch trailer. Wrap your iPhone recordings in a clean device frame. Add cinematic zoom moments to highlight what matters and export ready to post videos
for the app store, Twitter or product hunt. Open source, no watermarks, no subscription. The polish layer your indie app demos have been missing.
If you live inside Ghosty and run multiple coding agents at once, your window layout becomes chaos within minutes.
Rig is a small Mac OS sidecar for Ghosty that lets engineers create, focus, arrange, and track terminal sessions across projects and coding harnesses. It
controls real Ghosty Windows through Apple script and the Mac OS accessibility APIs. So, it's the actual
native terminal, not a fake one. Opting out of data brokers manually means filling the same form on 30 different
sites every few months forever. Auto identity remove runs playright against 30 plus people search sites on a monthly
schedule. Submits your opt- out requests automatically and logs everything.
Self-host on any machine or GitHub actions runs completely free. Your personal data quietly removed on autopilot.
Storing sensitive files in Dropbox or Google Drive means trusting the host with your encryption. Luxbox is a rustbased encrypted container that
mounts as a real drive on Linux, Mac OS, and Windows. Unlock with a passphrase, 502 hardware key, TPM 2.0, Windows
Hello, or hybrid postquantum key slots using MLKM 768 and 1024. Put the container in any cloud drive you want without trusting whoever runs it.
Kodif is a fast local diff viewer that runs on your desktop built specifically for reviewing AI generated code without
squinting at terminal output. The LLM walkthrough mode is the practical feature. Work through the diff, grab your review comments, paste them back to
Claude, and the fixes get applied directly. No context switching, no copy pasting between tools.
Ever wished JavaScript could run code at build time instead of shipping it to the browser? Comp time makes that real. It's
a Zigg inspired buildtime evaluation primitive for JavaScript exposed as plugins for Vite and roll down. Wrap any
expression and it gets evaluated during your build. Then the result gets inlined into the bundle. Shrink your output,
kill runtime cost and move expensive work to compile time.
You picked Postgress for your app. Then a year in you realize half your queries are relationship traversals that would be way faster in a graph database.
Pgraphph fixes that without making you migrate anything. It adds graph database superpowers directly on top of your
existing Postgress data. Run graph queries against the tables you already have. No separate Neo forj cluster to
operate. No double writing data. No sync pipeline.
Slopless is a TypeScript CLI that audits markdown files using 50 plus deterministic text lint rules, catching
overused buzzwords, forced transitions, and robotic cadence at zero API cost.
Output structured JSON so it wires cleanly into CI/CD pipelines or directly into writing agents like Claude Code.
Your agent writes a draft, slopless audits it, the agent rewrites until it passes. Automated slop detection that costs nothing per run.
Claude codes P flag gives you piped output but kills the interactive TUI in the process. Claude P fixes that by
driving the full interactive Claude code TUI inside an inprocess Zmux PTY session then capturing and streaming the output
cleanly. Same command, same flags, same muscle memory, scriptable piped output with the full interactive agent running underneath.
Most AI memory systems are vector databases with raw transcripts, noisy, bloated, and they still don't actually
know who you are. Elephant Agent does it differently. A personal model first architecture that builds a living model
of you, your relationships, your environment, your preferences. After every conversation, it reflects in the background and refines its internal map
of your life. So, its judgment gets sharper over time.
Yaki is a fully functional static HTTP web server written entirely in pure ARM 64 assembly for Mac OS. No external
libraries, no libc, raw Darwin sys calls directly to Apple silicon. Get, put, delete, bite range requests, custom
error pages, directory listing, slow loris mitigation, 48 kilob binary, over 1.2 million requests per second on an M3
while barely touching RAM. Technically impressive, existentially motivated, absolutely unhinged.
When your government shuts down the internet, regular VPNs get blocked first. White DNS takes a different approach. It's an Android DNS tunneling
client that smuggles your traffic through DNS queries. The one protocol firewalls usually can't kill. Two modes,
SOCK 5 proxy or a full system VPN using Android's VPN service with tontoroxy native libraries.
Pi is Armen Ronacher's coding agent platform. DS4 is antireez's pure metal inference engine for DeepSseek v4 flash.
PIDS4 is the bridge between them.
Install one PI provider extension and you get a local DeepSseek V4 flash model registered as DS4 Deepseek-V4J flash running entirely on Apple Silicon Metal.
Server starts on demand. Model downloads automatically. A watchdog shuts it down when no clients are left.
Want to ship a comic or manga reader as part of your web app without rolling your own page navigation, zoom, and
gesture handling from scratch? Kami is an open- source comic reader library for JavaScript and TypeScript. Drop it into
any web project. Point it at your image assets and you get a real comic reading experience with all the heavy lifting already done.
Jeepa is the reflective prompt optimizer from DSP that beats reinforcement learning with 35 times fewer rollouts.
But watching it work has been a wall of log files until now. Japa viz is an interactive live visualizer for Jeepa
runs. See the prompt evolution tree grow in real time. Watch the Pareto Frontier shift and inspect the natural language feedback driving each mutation.
Run any coding agent for more than an hour and watch it slowly forget what it was originally building. GSD PI is built
specifically to fix that. A metapar prompting context engineering and specdriven development system that keeps agents on track for long autonomous
runs. Instead of letting your agent improvise into chaos, you give it a structured spec and a context discipline that holds hour after hour.
Switching from claw code to cursor mid-p project usually means reexplaining everything from scratch. AI memory fixes that. It's a long-term memory layer for
AI coding CLIs that survives across vendors. Your project context, decisions, and history live in one
shared store, and any agent can pick up exactly where the last one left off. No more vendor lockin by virtue of memory loss.
AI agents rewrite functions with confidence and no awareness of what depends on them. Code index is a repo
dependency analyzer with blast radius impact scoring built specifically for AI assisted development. Before your agent
touches a file, it knows exactly what else will break. The blast radius score makes context light agents safer and
gives you a clear map of which files in your codebase are genuinely loadbearing.
AI generated markdown docs are thorough and unread. MD2 HTML is a portable skill for clawed code, codecs, and anti-gravity that converts long form
markdown into self-contained HTML pages people actually open. Mermaid diagrams, timelines, callouts, table of contents, multi- language support, all baked in.
No build step, no static site generator, one HTML file you can ship anywhere.
